(HQA) compiles frequently asked questions from patients before and during their hospital visits.

In this work, we proposed GiGPO, a novel group-based RL algorithm to tackle the credit assignment
challenge in long-horizon LLM agent training. GiGPO introduces a hierarchical advantage estimation
that enables fine-grained per-step credit assignment while retaining the efficiency and stability
of group-based RL. By retroactively grouping steps that share the same state across trajectories,
it achieves this without incurring additional LLM rollout or GPU memory overhead. Empirical
evaluations across complex agentic environments (ALFWorld and WebShop) and search-augmented
QA tasks demonstrate that GiGPO significantly outperforms both prompt-based agents and prior
